that was half victory party, half look ahead at how to deliver for voters. As NPR's Barbara Sprunt
reports, the event brought together rising stars, organizers, and lawmakers. Speaker after speaker
said Democrats can't rest on their laurels. Here's former transportation secretary Pete Buttigieg.
It is yet to be written whether what we just experienced is one more oscillation from one

politics. He said Democrats should come out of the gate strong with a rapid fire series of bills
to lower the cost of living. He was one of many potential presidential candidates in attendance,
all of whom said they're taking their time to decide before officially throwing their hat
in the ring. Barbara Sprunt and PR News, Denver. Microsoft says its products are back online after
a days-long outage knocked out critical services to companies and governments around the world.
And here's Marissa J. Lange has more. Two days after a massive outage shut down Microsoft
products like Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, its AI assistant, the company announced all services
had been restored to its more than 430 million customers. The outage affected international
government operations, healthcare services, businesses, banks, schools, courts, and even
the U.S. House of Representatives. In a post on X Friday, the technology company said it was deeply
sorry and described the outage as a technical issue. It said Microsoft was not the victim of
any cyber attacks or rogue AI agents, but instead blamed the failure on a network upgrade.
Marissa J. Lange, NPR News. And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
North Dakota last year became one of 29 states that limit how much patients with diabetes
have to pay for insulin. They capture support, bipartisan support.
Nome Levy with a partner at KFF Health News has more. Diabetes is expensive. Insulin can
cost patients hundreds or thousands of dollars, even if they have insurance. That's why some risk
rationing their insulin. Red states and blue are landing on a common fix. Cap how much patients
have to pay every month for the drug. Typically Republicans are more on the free market side of
things. Democrats are more supportive of intervening. But in this case, I think there is
broad agreement that this market just wasn't functioning. That's Republican Sean Cleary.
He's a North Dakota state senator who co-sponsored a state insulin cap.
Congress is now considering a national cap. Nome Levy with KFF Health News.

Authority says the feature violates a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law
that protects smartphones as part of a person's private sphere and requires free and informed

gallery access through a single permission that covered several apps. The fine was imposed on
